title: The Loose Deadline
premise: Felix Quintana, a sleepless interpreter for a doomed peace delegation in a fractured border city, answers a burner phone and hears the voice of Marisol, the woman she loved and lost to witness protection three years ago — except Marisol is supposed to be dead, killed in the 'incident' Felix can't remember clearly. The call drags Felix into a conspiracy spanning three governments: the peace talks are theater, the incident was staged, and Marisol is alive because she was its architect, now hunted by the assassin sent to erase loose ends. As dawn approaches, Felix must smuggle Marisol's evidence past intelligence officers on both sides of the table while the assassin closes in, forcing her to choose between the duty that defines her and the truth that could destroy her. In the end, Felix betrays neither side but exposes both — putting the recordings into the open at the airport itself — and escapes with Marisol on the extraction flight, though the price is her name, her career, and the identity she built to survive.
about_author: Casper Winterbourne is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in conflict zones before turning to fiction. Writing from a coastal town whose location they decline to confirm, they specialize in thrillers where language itself becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Insomnia
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Three days into failing peace talks, Felix translates a ceasefire clause she knows is a lie, haunted by fragmented memories of an explosion three years ago. She hasn't slept through a night since. Emotional beat: exhaustion masking dread; the reader feels her grip on reality fraying.

chapters.title: A Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A burner phone appears in her coat pocket — no sender, no explanation. When it rings at 3 a.m., the voice is Marisol's, the woman who died in the incident. Emotional beat: vertigo and longing colliding; Felix answers against every instinct of self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Dead Woman Wants
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (partial). From a safehouse, Marisol explains: the incident was staged, she faked her death, and she has recordings proving all three governments scripted the current talks' failure. She needs Felix's access and her languages. Emotional beat: old love weaponized into trust neither can afford.

chapters.title: The Delegation Dines
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At a diplomatic dinner, Felix notices details she once ignored: aides exchanging coded glances, a security chief whose accent doesn't match his file. She realizes the talks are designed to collapse on schedule. Emotional beat: disillusionment sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches Doors
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV, unnamed. The assassin reviews photographs of the delegation and flags Felix — not as a target yet, but as a thread worth pulling. He memorizes her routines. Emotional beat: cold patience; menace delivered through mundane professionalism.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Old Market
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. First physical contact with Marisol's network: a memory card hidden inside a spice tin, containing half the recordings. A tail follows Felix home; she loses him in the fish market using a trick Marisol taught her years ago. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into competence; muscle memory of love.

chapters.title: Three Flags, One Lie
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cross-referencing the recordings with delegation documents, Felix maps how each government benefits from the talks' failure. Her own employers are complicit. Emotional beat: betrayal of institution; duty begins to invert.

chapters.title: The Incident, Remembered
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, intercut with flashback. Triggered by a sound on the recording, Felix finally reconstructs the night of the explosion — and remembers Marisol pulling her out, then walking back toward the fire. Emotional beat: grief reframed; the insomnia breaks its silence.

chapters.title: Room 412
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Felix and Marisol meet face to face for the first time in three years, in a hotel room wired with the assassin's bugs they haven't found. They speak in overlapping languages to confuse the listeners. Emotional beat: tenderness under surveillance; intimacy as tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Bug
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. Listening to the hotel audio, the assassin catches one unguarded phrase and confirms Felix is compromised. He reports upward — and receives orders that make clear his own employers intend him to be expendable too. Emotional beat: first crack in the assassin's loyalty.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Courtesy
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A foreign intelligence officer invites Felix for 'informal coffee' and probes with exquisite politeness. Felix lies fluently in two languages, buying time but marking herself. Emotional beat: terror performed as calm; the cost of every sentence.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol admits the recordings implicate Felix's own father, a retired diplomat whose signature authorized the staging. She withheld it to protect her. Emotional beat: rage and heartbreak; trust nearly shatters over a mercy that felt like a lie.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Didn't Come
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Their plan to move the full archive via a network courier collapses when the courier turns up drowned. Felix realizes there's a leak inside Marisol's own circle. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in; no route left but the dangerous one.

chapters.title: Safehouse Burning
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The assassin raids the safehouse minutes after Marisol evacuates, finding only a photograph of Felix left deliberately behind — a message. He understands someone above him wants the two women to run somewhere predictable. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is also prey.

chapters.title: Running the River District
chapters.summary: Felix and Marisol's alternating POV. A night flight through flooded streets, pursued by both the assassin and government trackers. They argue about the father, about the past, about whether survival justifies anything. Emotional beat: love rekindled under fire, honest at last.

chapters.title: The Third Government
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix makes a desperate gambit: she walks into the consulate of the least implicated government and offers the recordings — not as a defector, but as leverage for protection. The consul listens longer than she expected. Emotional beat: audacity born of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Terms at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The assassin corners Marisol alone but doesn't shoot; instead he proposes an alliance — his employers will kill him once the archive surfaces, so he needs it surfaced too. Emotional beat: uneasy truce; enemy and asset in one body.

chapters.title: What Dawn Requires
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The extraction flight leaves at 6:10 a.m. from a military airfield. The plan: get Marisol aboard as delegation support staff using forged credentials only Felix can authorize — burning her own career in the process. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; the sacrifice named aloud.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the airfield gate, the forged papers fail inspection. The assassin creates a diversion that draws the guards, at the cost of his own escape route. Emotional beat: chaos compressed into seconds; debts paid in blood and nerve.

chapters.title: Broadcast Before Boarding
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. With minutes left, Felix does the unthinkable: instead of handing the archive to any government, she triggers its simultaneous release to press contacts in all three countries from the tarmac. Truth belongs to everyone or no one. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from ruin.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The plane lifts off as the city below erupts in scandal — resignations already being drafted. Marisol finds Felix in the cargo aisle, shaking, sleepless, free. Emotional beat: exhale after drowning; two survivors holding on.

chapters.title: The Loose Deadline
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, in an unnamed coastal town, Felix sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. She has no name on any roster now — only herself, and Marisol, and a morning that asks nothing of her. Emotional beat: identity surrendered and self reclaimed; the deadline met, the life begun.
